title: Edgecase PR salvage notes — quick heuristics and follow-ups
content:
Purpose:
This is my personal scratchpad for rescuing small-to-medium PRs that hit weird runtime/behavioral edge cases. Not a final postmortem — more of a triage checklist + quick fix sketches + followups. Use freely, copy pieces into PR comment or incident notes.

Context for current case (PR #4821):
- Changes introduced a subtle cache invalidation edge: rare client sequence lengths + kv-cache boundary lead to incorrect tokens on fallback. Behaviour seen in ~0.03% of requests in canary region A.
- Regression surfaced via customer error reports (slight hallucination on curated prompt set).
- Repro steps are noisy but reproducible locally with the attached test vectors (see linked artifact).

Immediate triage (first 60–90 minutes):
- 1) Stop new canary traffic to the variant (route -> fallback to stable model variant). Done via rollout console, note time.
- 2) Create minimal reproducer that runs in <2s on local GPU (reduce batch size, use the problematic token-length vector). Put under tests/regressions/pr-4821/replicator.py.
- 3) Capture 5 full failing traces (input + model state + first 128 tokens of kv-cache) and push to a temp S3 for analysis. Filename schema: pr4821/trace-<ts>-<id>.jsonl
- 4) Add temporary sampling rule so we capture any similar failures in prod for 24 hours (sample 1/1000).

Quick root-cause hypotheses (note-style):
- H1: cache slice alignment off-by-one when prefix length mod shard_size == 0 (highly plausible given code touched slice offsets).
- H2: interaction with quantized attention kernel when sequence length > configured_window (fallback path not updating cache metadata).
- H3: race between async KV flush and a hot-swap of weight shards during auto-scaling (less likely because failure doesn't correlate with scale events).

Sanity checks to rule in/out hypotheses (commands + minimal checks):
- Run unit test for slice math: python -m pytest tests/unit/test_kv_cache_offsets.py::test_offset_alignments -k "mod_boundary" -v
- Insert assert in runtime near cache write: assert cache.offset % shard == 0, f"offset:{cache.offset} shard:{shard}" (local only)
- Run reproduce with quantized vs fp16 kernel flag: \n  QUANT_KERNEL=1 python reproducer.py --local-kernel=quant && QUANT_KERNEL=0 python reproducer.py --local-kernel=fp16
- Check autoscale logs across timeframe of observed failures: gcloud logging read "resource.labels.instance_id=\"...\" AND timestamp>="2026-03-08T00:00:00Z"" --limit 1000

Quick mitigation options (ordered by speed / impact):
- Hotfix A (fast): Force fallback to stable kernel for the affected model variant for 48h. Pros: immediate mitigation. Cons: higher cost, not permanent.
- Hotfix B (fast-ish): Patch the offset calculation with a conservative guard (clamp + assert) and release patch to canary with heavy sampling. Example patch sketch:
  --- a/runtime/kv_cache.py
  +++ b/runtime/kv_cache.py
  @@ def write_slice(...):
  -    start = compute_offset(prefix_len)
  +    start = compute_offset(prefix_len)
  +    # defensive: clamp start to available buffer and log if we ever hit a clamp
  +    if start < 0 or start >= buffer_len:
  +        log.warn("kv-cache start out of bounds (clamped) prefix=%s start=%s buffer=%s", prefix_len, start, buffer_len)
  +        start = max(0, min(start, buffer_len - slice_len))

- Hotfix C (medium effort): Disable the async flush path for the affected kernel variant and switch to synchronous flush for those shards (costly perf-wise).

Rollback plan (if hotfix patch causes issues):
- Add a fast rollback PR that reverts the single hunk, test in canary for 30m, then flip route back to previous variant.
- Notify SRE + oncall with runbook: message in #prod-alerts with verbatim revert PR link and rollback command.

Testing matrix before re-release to stable:
- Unit tests: pass, add 3 new tests that exercise prefix_len edgecases (0, shard_size, shard_size*2 + 1).
- Integration smoke: run 1000 sample sequences with lengths sampled from production distribution (script: tests/regressions/benchmark_sequence_sampler.py).
- Latency/regression: run small perf sanity to ensure guard didn't add >2% tail latency.

Messaging (short templates to copy):
- PR comment to owner: "Spotted a rare cache alignment problem in canary. I've paused traffic, captured traces, and sketched two hotfix options (A: fallback kernel, B: defensive clamp). Can you take a look at compute_offset logic? I can iterate on a minimal patch and ship to canary today."
- Slack to #oncall: "[ENG] Paused variant A after 0.03% incorrect-token reports (PR 4821). Traces in s3://tmp/pr4821. Sampling up for 24h. Will post rollback link if we ship a fix."

Follow-up (post-fix) tickets (create after revert/patch lands):
- JIRA-9080: Add exhaustive kv-cache offset unit tests + property-based fuzzing (owner: Diego).
- JIRA-9081: Add perf benchmark for sync vs async flush to quantify cost of temporary sync-flush mitigation (owner: Ivy).
- JIRA-9082: Postmortem doc and customer outreach plan (owner: Ramona).

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Is there telemetry for cache.offset variance across requests? If not, add metric: runtime.kv_cache.offset_clamped_count (counter).
- Need to check whether the kernel selector uses a stale config cache in the edge case — could be a different root cause. Add audit log in kernel selector path.
- If we clamp, how will it affect generation determinism for replay tests? Add deterministic test harness.

Small nit fixes (things to do while waiting for tests):
- Add more verbose logging for the canary run: include prefix length, shard id, computed start, and kernel name (log level DEBUG).
- Tidy up reproducer: compress traces and redact PII before upload.

Action items (concrete next steps):
- Ramona: push hotfix patch sketch to branch ramona/pr4821-guard and open PR.
- Diego: add unit fuzzing ticket & start initial tests (JIRA-9080).
- Ivy: prepare perf microbenchmark for sync-flush tradeoff (JIRA-9081).
- Oncall: maintain sampling rule for 24h and escalate if >0.1% failures.

Misc scratch notes:
- If we can't reproduce reliably locally, try lowering the randomness seed and increasing batch to amplify state interplay.
- Consider a temporary canary-only feature flag that flips cache code path to a simpler pre-allocated buffer implementation to rule out allocator/fragmentation issues.

-- ramona (notes, 2026-03-10)

Unresolved for PR comment: should we include a tentative SLA credit offer line to impacted customers? flag: include-customer-template = false
